items.stem:
A train starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to 30 m/s in 60 s. It then travels at constant speed for 120 s before decelerating uniformly to rest in 40 s.

(a) Calculate the acceleration in the first phase.
(b) Calculate the total distance travelled.
(c) Sketch the velocity–time graph.
items.frontier: High-speed trains like the Japanese Shinkansen reach 83 m/s — what would the distance be at that speed for the same time?

items.stem: Discover how distance–time graphs reveal motion.
items.learn_content: A distance–time graph plots position against time. The **gradient (slope)** equals the **speed**. Steep = fast. Flat = stationary. The shape of the line tells the story of the journey.
learn_steps: If a line goes up steeply, what do you think that means?
If the line is completely flat, what is the object doing?
What would a downward slope mean on a *distance* vs time graph?
Now name it: gradient = speed = Δd / Δt
